title: Weighted IO split with streaming grace and enterprise SQ playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Our current per-token metering conflates ingress and egress in ways that penalize conversational customers with large context windows and penalizes streaming-first workloads. We want a practical experiment that: (1) evaluates weighted IO splits (different price per input vs output token), (2) measures the effect of a short streaming 'grace window' that exempts the first N streamed tokens from floor minimums to reduce churn for interactive apps, and (3) produces an enterprise Security Questionnaire (SQ) playbook that maps pricing changes to compliance and legal talking points for sales.

Goals: 
- Quantify revenue and unit-cost sensitivity for three candidate pricing variants across customer cohorts (chatbots, embeddings-heavy, batch transcription).
- Preserve predictability for enterprise contracts while incentivizing efficient prompts.
- Produce a concise SQ playbook for AEs and legal to reduce friction on renewals.

Experiment design: 
- Variant A (Baseline): current symmetric per-token rates, streaming subject to minimums.
- Variant B (Weighted IO): input tokens priced at 0.6x base; output tokens priced at 1.4x base (keeps expected bill neutral for long-form generation but reduces price for high-input workloads).
- Variant C (Grace Window + Buckets): apply Variant B rates, but for streaming sessions we waive the first 512 streamed output tokens from the session minimum; sessions also have a per-session micro-bucket (256 token credit) to smooth short bursts.

Key metrics (per-cohort):
- Revenue delta vs baseline (7, 30, 90 day windows)
- Unit cost per effective token (infrastructure cost model + KV cache hit adjustments)
- Churn propensity signal (usage drop >30% after price change, support tickets escalations)
- Median & 95th p99 latency change (to ensure no perverse scheduling incentives)

Data sources and assumptions: 
- Use telemetry from last 90 days segmented by model family and route.
- Cost model updated with recent kernel improvements (expected 8% cost reduction for long-sequence workloads).
- Assume 40% of streaming sessions are conversational (small-turn length) and 60% are long-form streaming (transcript).

Rollout plan: 
1) Simulated billing in staging for 4 weeks (billing projection model + customer-impact flags).
2) Small public pilot (5 customers across cohorts, opt-in) for 30 days.
3) Expand to a 10% random sample of traffic with guardrails (cancellation SLA for trial).

Enterprise SQ playbook: 
- One-page explainer that maps how weighted IO changes affect data residency, audit logs, and invoice structure.
- Scripts and templates for AEs explaining per-session credits, demonstrating examples for common contract sizes.
- Legal checklist for amendments (billing language, refund window for pilot, auditability of token metering).

Acceptance criteria: 
- Clear revenue + cost delta report with cohort breakouts and recommendation (go/no-go/partial).
- Pilot feedback from AEs and two enterprise customers with documented SQ signoff flow.
- Updated billing docs and SDK examples reflecting new rating logic.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Perverse prompt engineering to shift load between input and output tokens. Mitigation: telemetry-based anomaly detection and prompt-efficiency guidance in Console.
- Risk: Legal pushback on changing invoice granularity. Mitigation: offer a transition clause and 30-day opt-out for enterprise pilots.

Notes: this proposal intentionally biases toward protecting enterprise predictability while testing levers that reduce cost for high-input customers (e.g., retrieval-heavy apps).
